items.event_time_ist: Fri, Oct 9, 2026 (evening local ET; ~6:30 AM IST Oct 10)
items.title: Trump headlines Syracuse, NY rally for Blakeman's bid to unseat Hochul (catch-up, Oct 9)
items.summary: President Trump held a Friday-night rally at the Syracuse Oncenter on Oct 9, 2026 for Republican gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman's challenge to Gov. Kathy Hochul, missed by earlier sweeps. Boxing legend Mike Tyson flew in on Air Force One and took the stage ('there's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump'), along with Yankees president Randy Levine, Energy Secretary Chris Wright, EPA chief Lee Zeldin and House Republicans. Trump also endorsed NY House candidates Kailee Buller (NY-22, vs Rep. John Mannion) and Anthony Constantino (open NY-21), attacked Hochul on crime, immigration and energy bills, touted Micron's $100B NY semiconductor project, and closed with 'pretend I'm on the freaking ballot.' Blakeman framed the race as taxes/utility-bills/public-safety vs Hochul.

items.event_time_ist: Sat, Oct 10, 2026 (~3 PM CT / ~1:30 AM IST Oct 11)
items.title: Trump rallies Clarksville, TN for Hagerty and Blackburn with Kid Rock (catch-up, Oct 10)
items.summary: President Trump headlined a midterm rally at F&M Bank Arena in Clarksville, TN on Sat Oct 10, 2026 — a replacement stop after his planned Alabama-Georgia football-game appearance was dropped over storm safety (remnants of Hurricane Isaias). Kid Rock opened for ~4,500 supporters; Trump campaigned for Sen. Bill Hagerty's reelection and Marsha Blackburn's gubernatorial bid, repeated the $5,000 'Trump dividend' promise, touted the $6.6B Korea Zinc smelter (largest private investment in TN history) and Memphis crime-task-force operations, called Iranian leaders 'crazy,' and floated renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait' and an ocean the 'Trump Ocean.' His signature line: 'pretend. Just pretend that I'm running.'

items.title: CNN/AdImpact: GOP spending nearly 2x Dems on Senate TV ads but getting only ~40% more reach
items.summary: New CNN analysis of AdImpact data (published Oct 14): across nine competitive Senate races last month, Republicans outspent Democrats $233M to $121M on broadcast TV ads — nearly 100% more — but saw only about 40% more gross rating points. Republicans paid ~$274 per GRP vs $201 for Democrats; in some September races Democrats actually outpaced Republicans in GRPs entirely. Cause: ~9 in 10 GOP ad dollars flowed through outside groups paying elevated late-cycle rates, while Democratic campaigns used discounted candidate rates and earlier, cheaper reservations. Veteran GOP strategist John Thomas: Republicans are 'spending more to get less.' Follows the earlier-reported $682M-vs-$491M GOP ad-reservation advantage through Election Day.
